overview: This file concerns Japanese tonnage dues, customs formalities, and port-entry requirements, centering on the anomalous use of the U.S. Navy vessel U.S.S. Gold Star to carry privately owned commercial cargo between Japan and Guam. It combines a 1935 cross-reference concerning entry into unopened ports; a 1937 Kobe consular despatch with four documents from 1933 tracing the Gold Star dispute; State, Navy, Commerce, and Embassy correspondence that led the Navy to restrict the vessel to government cargo; and a separate inquiry concerning the S.S. Texas’s fueling stop at Yokohama. The bundle also contains an apparently misfiled fragment of a consular report on wartime aviation, shipping disruption, and anti-spy conditions in Taiwan.

people.role: Commander and captain of the U.S.S. Gold Star

people.name: McGinnis
people.role: Commander and executive officer of the U.S.S. Gold Star

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on entry into unopened Japanese ports
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a Japanese Embassy inquiry about American rules and charges governing entry into unopened and open ports.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japan's Embassy asks about special port-entry permission and tonnage-duty fees.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 196 on commercial cargo carried by the U.S.S. Gold Star
subfiles.from: Winthrop R. Scott, American Consul at Kobe
subfiles.about: Scott forwards a detailed account of the disputed carriage of commercial cargo from Japan to Guam by a U.S. Navy vessel.
subfiles.summary: Scott warns the Gold Star's tolerated but unregularized commercial cargo should be formalized given wartime conditions.

subfiles.title: Scott’s confidential letter to Cameron on the Gold Star dispute
subfiles.from: Winthrop R. Scott, American Consul at Kobe
subfiles.to: C. R. Cameron, American Consul General at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Scott reconstructs the Gold Star’s customs dispute from 1933 through 1937 and recommends either paying commercial dues or ending private shipments.
subfiles.summary: Scott recounts years of Japanese tolerance of the Gold Star's private cargo without dues, recommending formal permission and payment, or ending the practice.

subfiles.title: Unsigned Kobe Customs memorandum on warships carrying merchandise
subfiles.from: Official of the Kobe Custom House
subfiles.to: Commander of the U.S.S. Gold Star
subfiles.about: Kobe Customs states that a warship loading or unloading merchandise is liable to treatment as a merchant ship and to tonnage dues.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Kobe Customs waived dues this time, warning future Gold Star cargo would be taxed like a merchant vessel.

subfiles.title: Commander Faus’s request for assistance over threatened tonnage dues
subfiles.from: W. C. Faus, commanding the U.S.S. Gold Star
subfiles.about: Faus asks the consul to determine whether Japan will impose tonnage dues on the Gold Star at Kobe or other Japanese ports.
subfiles.summary: Faus asks if Japan's threatened tonnage dues are final, defending the Gold Star's cargo as benefiting Japan and warning Guam might reroute.

subfiles.title: Kobe Customs response on the Gold Star’s commercial cargo
subfiles.from: Tsutomu Kubotera, Director of Kobe Customs
subfiles.to: Howard Donovan, American Consul at Kobe
subfiles.about: Kubotera distinguishes the Gold Star’s immunity as a warship from the customs consequences of carrying general commercial goods.
subfiles.summary: Kobe Customs says the Gold Star's cargo trade technically counts as foreign trade, asking it stop carrying non-ship cargo.

subfiles.title: Garrels letter reporting a naval prohibition on cargo carriage
subfiles.to: Howard Donovan, American Consul at Kobe
subfiles.about: Garrels reports that the Gold Star’s commander had supposedly been instructed to obey regulations prohibiting U.S. naval vessels from transporting cargo.
subfiles.summary: Garrels reports the Navy ordered the Gold Star's captain to stop carrying commercial cargo per naval regulations.

subfiles.title: State Department letter requesting the Navy’s views on the Gold Star
subfiles.to: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: The State Department asks the Navy to resolve whether the Gold Star should pay commercial dues or stop carrying private cargo.
subfiles.summary: Hull asks the Navy's view on the Gold Star dispute, noting officials favor either paying dues or ending private cargo shipments.

subfiles.title: Telegram asking the Tokyo Embassy for its views
subfiles.about: The Department asks whether the Embassy was consulted about the Kobe despatch and whether it has comments before the issue is taken up with the Navy.
subfiles.summary: State asks Tokyo to confirm its involvement and opinion on the Gold Star dues dispute before consulting the Navy.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram recommending dues or an end to private freight
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.about: Grew states the Embassy’s position that the Gold Star should pay commercial dues or stop carrying freight for private parties.
subfiles.summary: Grew recommends either paying dues or ending the Gold Star's private freight, with the consul and attaché agreeing.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting verification of Japanese port-entry law
subfiles.about: The Department asks the Embassy to verify a claim that every ship stopping at Yokohama must enter and clear even when it only takes on fuel.
subfiles.summary: State asks Tokyo to verify whether the S.S. Texas needed formal entry despite only taking on bunker oil at Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Fragment of report on wartime conditions in Taiwan
subfiles.from: Alvin T. Rowe Jr., American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: This incomplete report describes military aviation, shipping disruption, property removal, and anti-spy intimidation in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Fragment: Taiwan sees reduced shipping amid wartime requisitioning and intense anti-spy suspicion hampering routine consular information-gathering.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram explaining Japanese tonnage and entry requirements
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.about: Grew confirms that foreign vessels entering Japanese ports for cargo, repairs, or fuel generally owe tonnage dues and must complete entry and clearance formalities.
subfiles.summary: Grew confirms Japan requires entry procedures and tonnage dues for all foreign vessels except those in genuine distress, matching the Texas case.

subfiles.title: Navy acknowledgment pending the Governor of Guam’s advice
subfiles.about: The Navy acknowledges the State Department’s Gold Star inquiry and postpones its opinion until the Governor of Guam responds.
subfiles.summary: Navy says it will await Guam's governor before giving its view on the Gold Star cargo dispute.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department request concerning the S.S. Texas
subfiles.from: J. M. Johnson, Assistant Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Commerce asks State to determine whether Japanese law required the S.S. Texas to enter and clear at Yokohama during a fueling-only stop.
subfiles.summary: Commerce asks State to verify Japan's entry-fee requirement for the S.S. Texas to resolve a pending petition.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Japanese law governing fueling stops
subfiles.from: Hugh R. Wilson, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Daniel C. Roper, Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: State forwards the Tokyo Embassy’s confirmation that fueling-only calls are ordinarily subject to Japanese tonnage dues and port formalities.
subfiles.summary: Wilson quotes the Embassy’s December 23 telegram in response to Commerce’s inquiry about the S.S. Texas. Foreign vessels visiting Japanese ports for cargo, repairs, or fueling must pay tonnage dues and enter and clear in the normal manner. Only disaster at sea or comparable unavoidable circumstances create an exemption.

subfiles.title: Navy decision restricting the Gold Star to government cargo
subfiles.from: William D. Leahy, Acting Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: The Navy announces that the Gold Star will carry only government cargo between Guam and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Navy orders the Gold Star to carry only government cargo between Guam and Japan, avoiding the dues dispute.

subfiles.title: Instruction to notify Japanese consulates of the Navy’s decision
subfiles.about: The Department transmits the Navy’s decision and instructs the Embassy to inform American consular offices in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Instruction directs the Embassy to notify Japanese consulates that the Gold Star will carry only government cargo.

interest: Shows a 1930s US-Japan dispute over commercial cargo on the naval supply ship Gold Star, testing warship immunity.
